summary.text: Mark Alford is the incumbent Republican U.S. Representative for Missouri's 4th District, first elected in 2022.
A Texas native and longtime television news anchor in Kansas City, he serves on the House Appropriations and Small Business committees and is seeking a third term with President Trump's endorsement.

paragraphs.text: Alford was born October 4, 1963, in Baytown, Texas, and graduated from Baytown Sterling High School in 1982.
According to Wikipedia, he studied government at the University of Texas at Austin but left without graduating.
He worked as a television reporter and anchor in Texas and Florida markets, including KPRC-TV in Houston, before joining WDAF-TV (Fox 4 News) in Kansas City in 1998.
His congressional website says he anchored Kansas City's morning news show for 25 years.

Ballotpedia lists his career experience as a team lead and realtor with ReeceNichols Real Estate and a team lead manager with VortexKC/Chartwell, and KCUR describes him as a former small-business owner and news anchor.
Alford announced his candidacy for Congress on October 27, 2021, won the Republican primary on August 2, 2022, and won that November's general election to succeed Rep. Vicky Hartzler.
He took office January 3, 2023, and was assigned to the Armed Services, Agriculture and Small Business committees in the 118th Congress.
In the 119th Congress he moved to the Appropriations Committee and remains on Small Business, where he chairs the Oversight and Investigations Subcommittee.
KCUR reports that he won more than 71% of the vote in both 2022 and 2024.
According to his congressional website, Alford is married to Leslie, they have three grown children, and he has raised money for charities and served on boards and civic organizations.
